nodes.label: Repo-wide regression gate (evals workflow)
nodes.rationale: Every skill's frozen acceptance-check is the durable residue of an already-fixed bug. Before this workflow, nothing ran those checks outside a whetstone run targeting that skill, so a fixed bug could silently come back — conductor's book-under-flag was fixed, verified, merged, then re-accreted across seven runs. The workflow therefore runs EVERY skill's floor and EVERY guarded check on every push and PR, not just the skill under work.

nodes.label: checks job — floors + frozen checks (fast gate)
nodes.rationale: Milliseconds-to-seconds per check, so it is the gate that must never be skipped; runs `node scripts/evals-all.mjs --fast` on node 22 with a 20-minute ceiling.
nodes.norm_label: checks job — floors + frozen checks (fast gate)

nodes.label: nets job — generator regression nets
nodes.rationale: Globs plugins/lirbox/skills/*/scripts/test-*.cjs and runs each, accumulating failures instead of bailing on the first, so one run reports every broken generator net. Split from the fast gate because arena's net clones fixture bundles and runs their npm suites, which would otherwise hold up the cheap checks.

nodes.label: Two-job split (fast gate vs slow nets)
nodes.rationale: Separating the slow generator nets (30-min timeout) from the fast floors+checks gate (20-min timeout) keeps the must-never-skip gate cheap and fast; concurrency is keyed on github.ref with cancel-in-progress so superseded pushes stop burning runners.
nodes.norm_label: two-job split (fast gate vs slow nets)

nodes.label: Two skill families (HTML-artifact vs orchestration/loop)
nodes.rationale: The repo's skills split into two shapes with different conventions: HTML-artifact skills emit one self-contained HTML file (and flowchart ships a headless validator to catch Mermaid label-escaping bugs), while orchestration/loop skills share one backbone — a deterministic JS conductor driving full-tool worker subagents. Knowing which family a skill belongs to decides which rules apply when editing it.

nodes.label: Conductor layer is pure JS — no fs/git/require/Date.now/Math.random
nodes.rationale: The generated loop .js must stay deterministic and side-effect-free so runs are reproducible and resumable; every side-effect lives inside an agent() worker prompt instead. The per-skill test-*.cjs enforce this mechanically with a string scan, so the rule cannot silently erode.
nodes.norm_label: conductor layer is pure js — no fs/git/require/date.now/math.random

nodes.label: Never hand-edit a generated loop script
nodes.rationale: Loop scripts come from scripts/scaffold-*.cjs; editing the output instead of the generator reintroduces drift between generator and artifact. The fix is always: change the generator, regenerate with --force.
nodes.norm_label: never hand-edit a generated loop script

nodes.label: Run the regression net after touching a generator
nodes.rationale: Each loop skill's test-*.cjs asserts loop/phase structure, the no-fs scan, and unit helpers — the mapping is conductor→test-scaffold.cjs, prospector→test-optimize.cjs, whetstone→test-improve.cjs, arena→test-arena.cjs. Running it is what makes a generator change safe.
nodes.norm_label: run the regression net after touching a generator

nodes.label: Non-destructive default — loops open PRs, never merge
nodes.rationale: prospector/whetstone finalize by auto-opening a PR with the run report as the body so a human reviews and merges; with no remote they fall back to leaving the branch. Run branches are per-run and timestamped (opt/<goal>-<ts>, improve/<skill>-<ts>) and keyed by run slug — not by skill/goal — so concurrent runs never collide on state/config/report/branch/worktree. The whetstone backlog stays keyed by skill (feedback/<skill>.jsonl).
nodes.norm_label: non-destructive default — loops open prs, never merge

nodes.label: Runtime artifacts are gitignored — never commit them
nodes.rationale: Per-run scratch (.workflows/, .optimize/, .improve/, .arena/, .worktrees/, generated *-flowchart/codewalk/plan-deck.html, implementation-notes/) is machine-local noise; committing it would pollute history with non-reproducible state.
nodes.norm_label: runtime artifacts are gitignored — never commit them

nodes.label: Delivery-artifact exception — docs/arena/** and docs/changes/** ARE committed
nodes.rationale: Scratch stays ignored, but promoted deliverables must ride the PR so a reviewer can read them: arena's Finalize promotes leaderboard.html + report.md into docs/arena/<name>/, and conductor's Writeup promotes kept implementation-notes/*.html plus writeup.html, design.html and the DocsGate summary.md into docs/changes/<name>/. .gitignore un-ignores both paths (!docs/arena/**, !docs/changes/**).
nodes.norm_label: delivery-artifact exception — docs/arena/** and docs/changes/** are committed

nodes.label: A skill's frontmatter description IS its trigger
nodes.rationale: The description is the only field that decides when Claude invokes the skill, so vagueness there costs invocations no amount of body quality recovers.
nodes.norm_label: a skill's frontmatter description is its trigger

nodes.norm_label: claude plugin validate . — pre-push marketplace validation

nodes.label: Skills resolve under the lirbox: namespace
nodes.norm_label: skills resolve under the lirbox: namespace

nodes.label: graphify query-first rule for codebase questions
nodes.rationale: graphify query/path/explain return a scoped subgraph that is usually far smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output, so querying first saves context; the wiki index serves broad navigation, GRAPH_REPORT.md only broad architecture review. `graphify update .` after code changes is AST-only and costs no API calls.
nodes.norm_label: graphify query-first rule for codebase questions

nodes.label: Add a new skill to the lirbox plugin (procedure)
nodes.rationale: Skills are auto-discovered from plugins/lirbox/skills/, so no manifest edit is needed: copy templates/skill-template, make `name` equal the kebab-case directory name, and put bundled resources in scripts/ (executable), references/ (loaded on demand to keep SKILL.md lean), assets/ (used in output, never loaded into context).
nodes.norm_label: add a new skill to the lirbox plugin (procedure)

nodes.label: Add a new agent to the lirbox plugin (procedure)
nodes.rationale: Agents are auto-discovered from plugins/lirbox/agents/*.md with frontmatter (name, description required; model and tools/permissions.allowedTools optional). Keep agents single-purpose — a tight role plus a clear output contract beats a broad one.
nodes.norm_label: add a new agent to the lirbox plugin (procedure)

nodes.label: Add a brand-new plugin to the marketplace (procedure)
nodes.rationale: Use a new plugin only when the work is a coherent product of its own rather than another tool in lirbox. Omit `version` during active development so updates track the git SHA — otherwise every release needs a bump or installed users never see changes. The new plugin must also be registered in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json with a name matching its plugin.json.
nodes.norm_label: add a brand-new plugin to the marketplace (procedure)

nodes.label: Marketplace layout rules (do not violate)
nodes.rationale: marketplace.json lives only at repo-root .claude-plugin/; a plugin's .claude-plugin/ holds only plugin.json — skills/, agents/, hooks/ sit at the plugin root, because nested under .claude-plugin/ they silently fail to load (the common mistake). All names kebab-case; runtime references go through ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, never absolute machine paths.

nodes.label: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} runtime path convention
nodes.rationale: Resolves to the installed plugin dir, so bundled scripts keep working after installation; absolute machine paths would only work on the author's box.

nodes.label: Enforced liemle3893 commit identity (pre-commit hook)
nodes.rationale: A machine's work git config must not leak into public history, so .githooks/pre-commit blocks any commit authored by the work account (liemlhd_msn / crownx / masangroup) or by anything other than the expected personal identity; contributors activate it once via git config core.hooksPath .githooks.

nodes.label: main is pull-request-only (ruleset + pre-push hook)
nodes.rationale: The GitHub ruleset requires a PR, requires both evals jobs green, and forbids force-push/deletion of main; its bypass list is empty so there is no admin escape hatch and loosening it is a visible ruleset edit. Reviews are deliberately not required (0 approvals) because a sole maintainer cannot approve their own PR — CI is the gate, not a rubber-stamp. .githooks/pre-push refuses the same push locally; --no-verify skips the hook but the server still rejects it. Loop run branches (improve/*, opt/*, wf/*, evals/*) stay unrestricted since they already finish by opening a PR.

nodes.label: Validate + smoke-test before pushing
nodes.rationale: `claude plugin validate .` schema-checks the marketplace and all plugins; `claude --plugin-dir ./plugins/lirbox` loads the plugin in a throwaway session so the skill/agent is exercised before it reaches installed users.

nodes.label: description is the single most important skill field
nodes.rationale: The model reads only name + description to decide whether to trigger a skill, so the description must be third-person and explicit about WHEN to use it.
nodes.norm_label: description is the single most important skill field

nodes.norm_label: lirbox — personal claude code plugin marketplace

nodes.label: Install + natural-language invocation examples
nodes.rationale: Skills are invoked by describing the task, not by naming them — the README's example phrasings double as documentation of each skill's trigger surface under the lirbox: namespace.

nodes.label: Omitting version makes updates track the git SHA
nodes.rationale: The lirbox plugin omits a pinned version, so Claude Code follows the commit SHA and pushing new commits is enough for installed users to pick up updates on /plugin marketplace update — no release bump ceremony.
nodes.norm_label: omitting version makes updates track the git sha

nodes.label: Test locally without installing (--plugin-dir / local marketplace)
nodes.norm_label: test locally without installing (--plugin-dir / local marketplace)

nodes.label: whetstone skill
nodes.rationale: Overnight, eval-gated skill improver on conductor's backbone: grinds a backlog through a deterministic floor plus a per-item acceptance-check (fail-before / pass-after), keeps only changes a check confirms, optionally compacts the skill, then opens a PR — never auto-merges.

nodes.label: flowchart skill
nodes.rationale: Turns a branching process into an interactive HTML flowchart (Mermaid decision diamonds + clickable per-node detail panel); renders via CDN so it needs internet.

nodes.label: sequence-diagram skill
nodes.rationale: Draws a time-ordered interaction as a self-contained interactive HTML sequence diagram — autonumbered Mermaid sequenceDiagram plus a numbered step list driving a clickable detail panel.

nodes.label: deep-understanding skill
nodes.rationale: Interactive tutor rather than a document: assesses what the human knows, fills gaps, quizzes problem → solution → impact, and does not stop until mastery is verified.

nodes.label: skill-lint skill
nodes.rationale: Deterministic analyzer aimed at the skills themselves — flags book-length SKILL.md files, unbalanced/missing XML structural tags, weak frontmatter triggers, oversized inline flowcharts and reference files. Reports ranked findings; never edits.

nodes.label: agent-template.md — agent authoring starter
nodes.rationale: Encodes the agent contract the orchestrator depends on: a frontmatter description specific enough to decide dispatch, a single clear responsibility, a Method section, and an explicit output contract.

nodes.label: Agent output contract convention
nodes.rationale: The caller needs a predictable return shape — a short status line or a fixed set of structured fields — with findings grounded in evidence (file:line, command output), nothing fabricated, and no scope expansion beyond the stated responsibility.

nodes.label: skill-template/SKILL.md — skill authoring starter
nodes.rationale: Fixes the SKILL.md shape every lirbox skill instantiates: third-person trigger description, When to use (including what it is NOT for so it doesn't fire on adjacent tasks), Inputs with defaults, imperative numbered Workflow, a verification step, and a Quality bar.

nodes.label: Bundled resources convention (scripts / references / assets)
nodes.rationale: Three directories with distinct context costs: scripts/ is deterministic runnable code that never enters context, references/ is loaded on demand to keep SKILL.md lean, assets/ feeds the skill's OUTPUT and is never loaded into context. Splitting this way is what keeps the always-loaded surface small.

nodes.label: Verify before claiming done (evidence before assertions)
nodes.rationale: Every skill must spell out the checks that prove its output is correct, so completion claims rest on evidence rather than on the model's confidence.
nodes.norm_label: verify before claiming done (evidence before assertions)
